candidates.title: Slots marked 'Few left' are pulled out of time order into an unlabelled block above Morning
candidates.description: Residents scan slots by time of day. On the slot list, every slot marked 'Few left' (for Saturday 17: 08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40, 10:20, 10:40, 13:40, 14:00, 15:00, 16:40) is shown first, in a block with no heading, above the 'Morning' heading; the remaining morning and afternoon slots follow under their headings with gaps where those slots were removed. So 08:00 sits under Morning while 08:20 sits above it, and afternoon slots appear above 'Morning'. The DOM/accessibility order is chronological, so keyboard focus moves from 08:00 (in the Morning block) back up to 08:20 (in the top block): the visual order and the focus/reading order disagree.
candidates.impact: A resident looking for 'Saturday morning' may conclude from the Morning row that only 08:00, 09:20 and 10:00 are free, missing nine free morning slots. A keyboard or screen-magnifier user sees focus jump between distant blocks, and a sighted keyboard user cannot predict where Tab goes.

evidence.detail: Few-left block above 'Morning' heading, mixing 08:20 and 16:40
Same ordering at 1280
group 'Slots': heading Morning, then buttons 08:00, 08:20 Few left, 08:40 Few left... in chronological order
After Tab from 'Another day', 08:00 is focused (expect passed); next Tab focuses '08:20 Few left', which is visually above the Morning heading
Same pattern for Monday 12 October via Another day

factor_notes.frequency: Every day view that has any 'Few left' slot; all viewports
factor_notes.impact: Misreads availability by time of day; disorients keyboard users
factor_notes.persistence: Recurs on every visit and every day change

candidates.recommendation: Keep slots in time order under Morning/Afternoon and show 'Few left' as a badge in place.

candidates.title: Slot buttons show no visible keyboard focus indicator
candidates.description: Keyboard-only residents need to see which slot has focus before pressing Enter. In a probe, focus was confirmed on the 08:00 slot and then on the 08:20 slot (expect state=focused passed), yet the screenshots of both steps are identical: neither button shows an outline, ring or other change. The day-entry text field, by contrast, shows a thick focus ring.
candidates.impact: Context lists keyboard-only booking among older residents. Without a focus indicator on the 29 slot buttons they cannot tell which time they are about to choose, and may book the wrong slot or give up.

evidence.detail: steps 5 and 8: expect role=button[name='08:00'] focused, then role=button[name='08:20 Few left'] focused, both ok
08:00 focused, no visible indicator
08:20 focused, no visible indicator; identical to step-06
Text field 'Day' shows a visible focus ring, for comparison

factor_notes.impact: Cannot locate focus among a grid of 29 similar buttons

candidates.recommendation: Give .slot buttons a clearly visible :focus-visible outline consistent with the text field.

candidates.title: Slot area stays blank for over a second after choosing a day, with no loading indication
candidates.description: After clicking a day button the 'Slots' heading is followed by empty space and the Next button; no 'Loading' text, spinner or live message appears. In a probe the slot buttons became visible 1284 ms after clicking 'Saturday 17'. The persona notes residents do not know that the slots take a moment to appear.
candidates.impact: On a phone, a blank area under 'Slots' with Next directly below may read as 'no slots' or a broken page; residents may press Next (which then asks them to choose a slot) or switch days. Screen-reader users get no status announcement during the wait.

evidence.detail: Immediately after clicking Saturday 17: 'Slots' heading, empty area, Next button
step 2 wait .slot visible took 1284 ms

factor_notes.impact: Short wait but ambiguous empty state

candidates.title: Change slot and Back to the slots reopen step 1 on Today instead of the chosen day
candidates.description: When a resident goes back to change the time, the slot page should open on the day and slot already chosen. Both 'Change slot' on the confirm page and 'Back to the slots' on the vehicle page link to index.html with no state: the page opens with 'Today' pressed, 'Monday 12 October' slots listed and no slot selected, although the booking is for Saturday 17 at 09:20. The resident must find and re-select Saturday before choosing 14:20. (Vehicle, waste and registration are kept: after re-selecting, Next went straight to the confirm page with Car, Garden waste, Wood and AB12 CDE intact.)
candidates.impact: In the change-slot journey a resident on a phone must remember which day they had chosen and re-select it; a resident who does not notice the reset may pick 14:20 on Monday instead of Saturday.

evidence.detail: After Change slot from Saturday 17 09:20: button 'Today' [pressed], paragraph 'Monday 12 October', no slot pressed; final_url index.html
After Back to the slots: 'Today' [pressed], 'Monday 12 October'
After re-selecting Saturday 17 and 14:20, confirm page keeps Car, Garden waste, Wood and registration

candidates.title: Permit number field is shown and unlabelled as optional when Car is chosen
candidates.description: Only vans and cars with trailers need a permit. On the vehicle step the 'Permit number' field with hint 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.' is visible before any vehicle is chosen and stays visible after choosing 'Car'. Nothing near the field says it applies only to vans and trailers; that rule is only inside the collapsed 'About vans and trailers' panel and in the Opening days text on step 1.
candidates.impact: Car drivers, the primary group, may believe they need a permit they do not have and abandon the booking or call the council.

candidates.title: Choosing Van without a permit passes the vehicle step; the error appears only after all personal details are entered
candidates.description: A missing permit should be caught on the step where the vehicle and permit are entered. With 'Van' chosen and the permit field empty, Next on the vehicle step goes straight to 'Check and book', which shows 'Van, no permit given' without any warning. Only after filling registration, name, mobile and postcode and pressing 'Book this slot' does an error appear: 'A van needs a permit number (DRC- and five digits).' Unlike the other summary errors, this item is plain text, not a link to the field, and the permit field is not on that page.
candidates.impact: Van and trailer owners, who are the ones turned away at the gate for wrong vehicle details, discover the problem last, must find 'Change vehicle' themselves, and may not have the permit to hand.

candidates.title: 'Slot no longer available' error does not say what to do and leaves 'Book this slot' active
candidates.description: When the held slot expires, the confirm page shows 'There is a problem: This slot is no longer available.' The message is not a link, does not say to choose another slot or how, and does not name which slot was lost; the summary's Slot row now reads only '—'. 'Book this slot' remains as the primary button although there is no slot. Entered details are kept.
candidates.impact: A resident who has just typed all details is told the booking failed without a next step; on a phone they may press 'Book this slot' again or start over from the header, unsure whether the details survive.

candidates.title: No indication anywhere that a chosen slot is held only for a limited time
candidates.description: The persona does not know how long a chosen slot is held, and the slot can expire before booking (expired state). Searched: step 1 (default, date-chosen, slot-chosen), vehicle step (default, van, info-open, errors) and confirm step (default, errors) ARIA snapshots and screenshots at 375 and 1280. None shows a hold duration, a countdown or a statement that the slot is not yet reserved; the only related text appears after expiry ('This slot is no longer available').
candidates.impact: Residents booking while doing something else (context of use) may pause between steps and lose the slot without warning, and users who type slowly or use assistive technology have no chance to ask for more time.

candidates.title: No online way to change or cancel an existing booking by reference
candidates.description: Residents changing a booking know their reference. Searched: header navigation (Book a slot, Opening days) on all routes; step 1 default; confirm page; done page booked and cancelled states; footer. None offers a 'Change or cancel a booking' entry or a reference field. The done page says only 'If you cannot come, call 01632 960771 on a weekday', and the footer gives phone hours weekdays 09:00 to 17:00, while the centre opens every day except Wednesday.
candidates.impact: Residents who need to move a weekend slot on Friday evening or at the weekend cannot do it; others may book a second slot (limit two per week) instead of moving the first, and phone-only access excludes residents who cannot use the phone.

candidates.title: Permit help says 'Apply on the council site' without a link
candidates.description: The 'About vans and trailers' panel explains that a free permit is needed and says 'Apply on the council site; it comes by email within two working days.' There is no link or address for where to apply. The van/trailer user group explicitly does not know where the permit number comes from.
candidates.impact: Van and trailer owners without a permit have to search the council site, and may not realise the two-day delay rules out a booking for tomorrow.
